## Classifying commands

The gateway has to know whether a command reads or writes before it can
choose a lock.
[`classify`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#classify)
sorts a Git argument list into one of three kinds. `read` commands, such
as `status` and `log`, share a lock and run with `--no-optional-locks`,
which stops Git from rewriting its index file in passing. `write`
commands take the lock alone. `net` commands
([`clone`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#clone),
`fetch`, `ls-remote` and `push`) use a separate lock.

Some commands read or write depending on their arguments:
`git branch --list` reads but `git branch -d x` writes. The `MIXED`
table lists, for each such command, the arguments that make it a read. A
command
[`classify`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#classify)
does not recognise counts as a write. That costs a little concurrency,
but it means an unknown command that changes the repository never runs
alongside another.

``` python
test_eq(classify(('status', '--porcelain=v1')), 'read')
test_eq(classify(('add', '--', 'x.py')), 'write')
test_eq(classify(('fetch', 'origin')), 'net')

test_eq(classify(('branch', '--show-current')), 'read')
test_eq(classify(('config', '--get=x')), 'read')        # `--opt=value` is read by its stem
test_eq(classify(('config', 'user.name', 'x')), 'write')
test_eq(classify(('worktree', 'list')), 'read')
test_eq(classify(('worktree', 'add', 'x')), 'write')
test_eq(classify(('symbolic-ref', 'HEAD')), 'read')     # one argument reads, two write
test_eq(classify(('symbolic-ref', 'HEAD', 'refs/heads/x')), 'write')
test_eq(classify(('-C', '/tmp', 'status')), 'read')     # a global option, then the subcommand
test_eq(classify(('--no-pager', 'log')), 'read')
test_eq(classify(()), 'write')                          # unreadable, so pessimistic
test_eq(classify(('sneak',)), 'write')
test_eq(classify(('commit-tree', 'x')), 'read')         # writes an object, touches no ref
```

## Locking one repository

[`RepoLock`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#repolock) is
a readers-writer lock: any number of readers at once, or one writer
alone. The thread holding the write lock can take it again and can also
read, so a change can inspect its own result without waiting on itself.
The `net` lock is separate because network commands do not touch the
index or the working tree.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L70"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### RepoLock

``` python
def RepoLock():
```

*A per-repository readers-writer lock, reentrant for the thread holding
the write.*

``` python
lock = RepoLock()
with lock.read():
    with lock.read(): pass                              # readers do not exclude each other
with lock.write():
    with lock.write(): pass                             # the writing thread is reentrant
    with lock.read(): pass                              # ...and may read inside its own write

seen = []
def reader():
    with lock.read(): seen.append('read')
with lock.write():
    t = threading.Thread(target=reader); t.start(); t.join(.2)
    test_eq(seen, [])                                   # a writer excludes a reader in another thread
t.join(2)
test_eq(seen, ['read'])

held = threading.Event()
def netter():
    with lock.net(): held.set(); time.sleep(.05)
t = threading.Thread(target=netter); t.start()
held.wait(2)
with lock.read(): pass                                  # ...but the network lock does not
t.join(2)
```

## Recovery state

A
[`Safepoint`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#safepoint)
records where a repository was just before one change: the commit `HEAD`
pointed at, the current branch, the commit holding a snapshot of
uncommitted work (empty when there was none), how many files were
uncommitted, the token that names it, and the time. Safepoints are kept
as refs under `refs/leela/safepoint/` and listed in a journal file
inside `.git`. An ordinary push does not send either, so they stay on
your machine. `describe` returns one line such as
`merge on main, 2 uncommitted file(s) kept`.

`SAFEPOINT_REF` and `JOURNAL_NAME` still say `leela`, the editor this
module was written for. Renaming them would lose track of safepoints
already on disk.

`FOREIGN_LOCK` matches the errors Git prints when another process, such
as a terminal or another editor, is holding one of Git’s lock files. The
gateway retries those commands a few times, with a growing pause, before
it gives up.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L120"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Safepoint

``` python
def Safepoint(
    token:str, op:str, head:str, branch:str, stash:str, dirty:int, created_at:int
)->None:
```

*Where a repository was just before one change: its commit, its branch
and a snapshot of uncommitted work.*

``` python
p = Safepoint(token='a1', op='merge', head='abcdef1234', branch='main', stash='', dirty=0, created_at=0)
test_eq(p.describe(), 'merge on main')
test_eq(Safepoint('a1', 'rebase', 'abcdef1234', '', '', 0, 0).describe(), 'rebase on abcdef123 (detached)')
test_eq(Safepoint('a1', 'commit', '', '', '', 0, 0).describe(), 'commit on an unborn branch')
test_eq(Safepoint('a1', 'merge', 'abcdef1234', 'main', 'x', 2, 0).describe(),
        'merge on main, 2 uncommitted file(s) kept')

assert FOREIGN_LOCK.search("fatal: Unable to create '/r/.git/index.lock': File exists")
assert FOREIGN_LOCK.search('Another git process seems to be running in this repository')
assert not FOREIGN_LOCK.search('fatal: not a git repository')
```

## The Git gateway

[`GitGateway`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#gitgateway)
runs Git commands under the right repository lock. The locks only
protect anything if every caller shares one gateway, so use
[`gateway()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#gateway) to
get the process-wide instance rather than creating your own. The checks
on this page create private gateways only so they can test them.

The gateway also caches, for some seconds, values that change less often
than the files. `memo(cwd, key, make, ttl)` caches any value per
repository. `env_for` lets an application choose the environment
variables Git runs with in each checkout, for example to put the
project’s virtual environment on `PATH` so Git can find a filter program
installed there. When `env_for` is `None`, Git inherits the process’s
environment. `resolves` finds the program a filter or hook command would
run, using that `PATH`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L134"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitGateway

``` python
def GitGateway():
```

*Run Git with shared repository locks, cached environments, and recovery
journals.*

``` python
gw = GitGateway()
r = mkrepo()
test_eq(gw._lock(r) is gw._lock(r), True)               # one lock per root, shared across callers
test_ne(gw._lock(r), gw._lock(mkrepo()))
assert gw._git().endswith('git')

calls = []
def make(): calls.append(1); return len(calls)
test_eq(gw.memo(r, 'k', make), 1)
test_eq(gw.memo(r, 'k', make), 1)                       # inside the ttl, the answer is not remade
test_eq(gw.memo(r, 'k', make, ttl=-1), 2)               # ...and outside it, it is
test_eq(gw.memo(r, 'other', make), 3)                   # keyed by (root, key)

test_eq(gw.env(r), None)                                # no `env_for` wired in: inherit the process
gw.env_for = lambda cwd: {'PATH': '/nowhere'}
test_eq(gw.env(r), {'PATH': '/nowhere'})
test_eq(gw.resolves(r, 'jupyter'), '')                  # not on that PATH
test_eq(gw.resolves(r, ''), '')
test_eq(gw.resolves(r, 'a "b'), '')                     # unparseable, not a crash
gw.env_for = None
```

## Running a command

[`GitGateway.run`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#gitgateway.run)
is the only function in this module that starts Git. It takes the lock
[`classify`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#classify)
chooses, or the one named by `kind`, and runs the command with a 30
second timeout by default. When Git fails because another process holds
one of its lock files, `run` tries again, up to four times in all, with
a growing pause between tries. A failed command raises
[`GitError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#giterror),
with both stderr and stdout in the message because Git prints useful
text on either. With `check=False` it returns the failed result instead.
`out` is `run` returning only stdout. Git’s stdin is `input` when given
and `/dev/null` otherwise, so Git never shares the caller’s terminal.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L209"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
gw, r = GitGateway(), mkrepo()
test_eq(gw.out(r, 'branch', '--show-current').strip(), 'main')
test_eq(gw.run(r, 'status', '--porcelain=v1').stdout, '')
test_eq(gw.run(r, 'rev-parse', 'nope', check=False).returncode != 0, True)   # check=False reports
test_fail(lambda: gw.run(r, 'rev-parse', 'nope'), contains='nope')           # ...and check=True raises
test_fail(lambda: gw.run(r, 'checkout', 'nope'), contains='did not match')

write(r, 'readme.md', 'changed\n')
test_eq(gw.out(r, 'status', '--porcelain=v1').rstrip(), ' M readme.md')
test_eq(gw.run(r, 'add', '-A', kind='write').returncode, 0)                  # an explicit kind wins
test_eq(gw.out(r, 'status', '--porcelain=v1').rstrip(), 'M  readme.md')

# stdin reaches the command, which is how a patch is applied.
test_eq(gw.run(r, 'hash-object', '-w', '--stdin', input='x\n').stdout.strip()[:2].isalnum(), True)
test_fail(lambda: gw.run(r, 'log', '--format=%H', timeout=0), contains='timed out')
# Without `input`, stdin is end of file, and a line waiting on the caller's terminal stays there.
import os, pty, sys
m, s = pty.openpty(); os.write(m, b'x\n')
probe = f"import os, select; from gheasy.repo import GitGateway; print(GitGateway().out({str(r)!r}, 'hash-object', '--stdin').strip(), os.read(0, 9) if select.select([0], [], [], 1)[0] else b'')"
got = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', probe], stdin=s, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60).stdout.split()
os.close(s); os.close(m)
test_eq(got, ['e69de29bb2d1d6434b8b29ae775ad8c2e48c5391', "b'x\\n'"])
```

## Recording recovery points

The journal is a JSON file inside `.git` that lists safepoints newest
first, keeping the latest `JOURNAL_KEEP` (60). It is written to a
temporary file and renamed into place, so a reader never sees half a
file. A journal that cannot be read or written never stops a Git
command; one that cannot be read counts as empty.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L226"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitGateway.journal

``` python
def journal(
    root
):
```

*Safepoints for this repository, newest first.*

``` python
gw, r = GitGateway(), mkrepo()
test_eq(gw._git_dir(r), r/'.git')
test_eq(gw._journal_path(r), r/'.git'/JOURNAL_NAME)
test_eq(gw.journal(r), [])                              # no file yet

for i in range(3): gw._record(r, Safepoint(f't{i}', 'op', 'a'*40, 'main', '', 0, i))
test_eq([p.token for p in gw.journal(r)], ['t2', 't1', 't0'])    # newest first

for i in range(JOURNAL_KEEP + 5): gw._record(r, Safepoint(f'x{i}', 'op', 'a'*40, 'main', '', 0, i))
test_eq(len(gw.journal(r)), JOURNAL_KEEP)               # capped, oldest dropped

gw._journal_path(r).write_text('not json')
test_eq(gw.journal(r), [])                              # unreadable reads as empty, never raises
gw._journal_path(r).write_text('[1, 2, {"token": "ok", "op": "o", "head": "h", "branch": "b", '
                               '"stash": "", "dirty": 0, "created_at": 0}]')
test_eq([p.token for p in gw.journal(r)], ['ok'])       # non-object rows are skipped
```

## Creating a safepoint

`safepoint` captures uncommitted work with `git stash create`, which
builds a stash commit without touching your files or adding to the stash
list. It then points refs at that commit and at `HEAD`, so Git’s garbage
collection keeps both. It returns `None` on a branch with no commits
yet, where there is nothing to return to. `transaction` holds the
repository’s write lock for a whole operation and records the safepoint
before the operation starts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

``` python
def transaction(
    root, op, snapshot:bool=True
):
```

*Hold the write lock for a whole operation, recording a safepoint first
unless `snapshot` is false.*

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitGateway.safepoint

``` python
def safepoint(
    root, op
):
```

*Record where the repository is, without changing it, and return the
[`Safepoint`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#safepoint),
or `None` on a branch with no commits.*

``` python
gw, r = GitGateway(), mkrepo()
base = sh(r, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD')
write(r, 'readme.md', 'dirty\n')
p = gw.safepoint(r, 'demo')
test_eq((p.op, p.branch, p.dirty, p.head), ('demo', 'main', 1, base))
test_eq((r/'readme.md').read_text(), 'dirty\n')         # snapshotting does not clean the tree
assert p.stash
test_eq(sh(r, 'rev-parse', f'{SAFEPOINT_REF}/{p.token}/head'), base)
test_eq([x.token for x in gw.journal(r)], [p.token])    # ...and it is journalled

with gw.transaction(r, 'held') as point: test_eq(point.op, 'held')
with gw.transaction(r, 'held', snapshot=False) as point: test_eq(point, None)
```

## Restoring a safepoint

`undo` first aborts any merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert in
progress. It then switches back to the recorded branch, resets it to the
recorded commit, and reapplies the saved uncommitted work. Without a
token it restores the newest safepoint.

If the saved work no longer applies cleanly, `undo` raises
[`GitError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#giterror),
but the work stays reachable as a commit and the message gives the
`git stash apply` command that recovers it. `undo` never discards that
work. `active_operation` names the operation in progress, or returns an
empty string.

[`gateway()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#gateway)
returns the process-wide
[`GitGateway`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#gitgateway).

``` python
test_fail(lambda: gw.undo(r, 'nosuch'), contains='no safepoint nosuch')
test_fail(lambda: gw.undo(mkrepo()), contains='nothing to undo')
```

## Finding and cloning repositories

[`repo_root`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/core.html#repo_root)
returns the top folder of the checkout that contains a path, or `None`
outside any repository.
[`url_name`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#url_name)
gives the folder name a clone of a URL gets.
[`clone_target`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#clone_target)
works out where a clone would land and refuses anything risky: a URL
starting with `-`, which Git would read as an option, a name containing
`/`, a parent that is not a folder, or a target that already exists.
[`clone`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#clone) makes
the same checks, clones, and returns the new folder.

``` python
test_eq(made, parent/'copy')
test_eq(repo_root(made), made.resolve())
```

## Parsing conflict markers

When Git cannot combine two changes to the same lines, it writes both
into the file between conflict markers: `<<<<<<<` opens the block,
`=======` separates our side from theirs, and `>>>>>>>` closes it.
[`_conflict_blocks`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#_conflict_blocks)
finds each complete block and returns where it starts and ends and the
text of both sides. A marker sequence with a part missing is left as
ordinary text.

``` python
block, = _conflict_blocks('a\n<<<<<<< HEAD\nx\n=======\ny\n>>>>>>> o\nb\n')
test_eq((block['ours'], block['theirs']), ('x\n', 'y\n'))
test_eq(block['start'], 2)

test_eq(_conflict_blocks('nothing here\n'), [])
test_eq(_conflict_blocks('<<<<<<< HEAD\nx\nno middle\n'), [])       # malformed stays text
test_eq(_conflict_blocks('<<<<<<< HEAD\nx\n=======\ny\n'), [])      # no closing marker
test_eq(len(_conflict_blocks('<<<<<<< a\n1\n=======\n2\n>>>>>>> b\n'
                             '<<<<<<< a\n3\n=======\n4\n>>>>>>> b\n')), 2)
test_eq(_conflict_blocks('<<<<<<< a\n\n=======\n\n>>>>>>> b\n')[0]['ours'], '\n')
```

## Short-lived status caching

An editor’s file tree can ask for the status of the same repository
several times in one refresh.
[`_cached`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#_cached)
shares one answer for `_CACHE_TTL` seconds, under half a second.
`invalidate(root)` drops every cached answer for a repository, and each
method that changes the repository calls it. An answer that was still
being worked out when
[`invalidate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#invalidate)
ran is not stored, so a stale result cannot slip back into the cache.
`changes`, which an editor calls right after saving a file, never uses
the cache.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L391"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### invalidate

``` python
def invalidate(
    root
):
```

*Drop every cached answer for `root`, after something wrote to it.*

``` python
calls = []
def make(): calls.append(1); return len(calls)
root = '/some/root'
test_eq(_cached(root, 'k', make), 1)
test_eq(_cached(root, 'k', make), 1)                    # inside the ttl
test_eq(_cached('/other', 'k', make), 2)                # keyed by root as well as key
invalidate(root)
test_eq(_cached(root, 'k', make), 3)                    # a mutation drops what it invalidated
test_eq(_cached('/other', 'k', make), 2)                # ...and only that root
invalidate('/other')
```

## Small helpers

Parsers for the status and branch readers, and three text helpers used
across the module.
[`plural`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#plural) writes
a count with the right form of a noun,
[`shorten`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#shorten)
collapses whitespace and cuts text to a length, and
[`unborn`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#unborn) says
whether an object id is Git’s all-zero id, which stands for a commit

``` python
test_eq(_remote_web_url('git@github.com:o/r.git'), 'https://github.com/o/r')
test_eq(_remote_web_url('ssh://git@github.com/o/r.git'), 'https://github.com/o/r')
test_eq(_remote_web_url('git://github.com/o/r.git'), 'https://github.com/o/r')
test_eq(_remote_web_url('https://github.com/o/r/'), 'https://github.com/o/r')
test_eq(_remote_web_url('/local/path'), '')             # nothing a browser could open
test_eq(_remote_web_url(''), '')

test_eq(_track_counts('[ahead 2, behind 1]'), (2, 1))
test_eq(_track_counts('[ahead 3]'), (3, 0))
test_eq(_track_counts(''), (0, 0))
test_eq(_track_counts('[gone]'), (0, 0))

test_eq(plural(1, 'file'), '1 file')
test_eq(plural(0, 'file'), '0 files')

test_eq(shorten('a  b   c', 4), 'a b…')
test_eq(shorten('short', 40), 'short')
test_eq(shorten(None, 4), '')

assert unborn('0' * 40)
assert not unborn('0' * 39 + '1')

test_eq(_fields('a\0b', 4), ['a', 'b', '', ''])         # padded to the width asked for
test_eq(_fields('a\0b\0c', 2), ['a', 'b'])              # ...and truncated to it
```

## Reporting outcomes

Every guarded change returns the same dictionary, described under
“Mutation results” below, and
[`_summarise`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#_summarise)
turns it into one sentence for a person. A conflict comes first, because
it is what needs dealing with, then an operation still in progress, then
files staged but not yet committed.

[`_explain_filters`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#_explain_filters)
explains filters that cannot run. A filter is a program, named in
`.gitattributes`, that Git runs on a file as it is staged and checked
out; nbstripout, which strips outputs from notebooks, is a common one.

``` python
base = {'op': 'merge', 'staged': [], 'conflicted': [], 'moved': False, 'head': 'abc1234',
        'message': '', 'operation': {'active': ''}}
test_eq(_summarise(base), 'merge changed nothing')
test_eq(_summarise(base | {'moved': True}), 'merge moved this branch to abc1234')
test_eq(_summarise(base | {'staged': ['a']}), 'merge staged 1 file without committing -- commit to finish')
test_eq(_summarise(base | {'operation': {'active': 'rebase'}}),
        'rebase is in progress -- continue, skip, or abort it')
test_eq(_summarise(base | {'conflicted': ['a', 'b']}),
        'merge stopped at 2 conflicted files -- resolve them to continue')
test_eq(_summarise(base | {'message': 'Already up to date.\nmore'}), 'Already up to date.')
# a conflict outranks everything else, because it is what the person has to deal with
test_eq(_summarise(base | {'conflicted': ['a'], 'staged': ['a'], 'moved': True}),
        'merge stopped at 1 conflicted file -- resolve them to continue')

assert 'cannot be found' in _explain_filters([{'name': 'nbstripout', 'configured': True,
                                               'clean': 'nbstripout', 'smudge': ''}])
assert 'configured nowhere' in _explain_filters([{'name': 'lfs', 'configured': False,
                                                  'clean': '', 'smudge': ''}])
test_eq(_explain_filters([]), '')
```

## Reading a diff

Git’s machine-readable diff output separates fields with NUL characters
and writes a renamed file as three fields rather than two, which a
simple two-field parse gets wrong.
[`_diff_status`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#_diff_status)
and
[`_diff_numstat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#_diff_numstat)
handle renames, and both keep `None` line counts for a binary file
rather than reporting zero lines changed.
[`_unified`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#_unified)
makes a unified diff of two strings, for files Git has no earlier
version of.

``` python
test_eq(_unified_arg(3), '--unified=3')
test_eq(_unified_arg(-1), '--unified=0')                # clamped both ways
test_eq(_unified_arg(999), '--unified=20')

d = _unified('a\n', 'b\n', 'a/x', 'b/x')
assert d.startswith('--- a/x') and '-a' in d and '+b' in d
test_eq(_unified('same\n', 'same\n', 'a', 'b'), '')

rows = _diff_status('M\0a.py\0R090\0old.py\0new.py\0A\0c.py\0')
test_eq([r['path'] for r in rows], ['a.py', 'new.py', 'c.py'])
test_eq(rows[1]['old_path'], 'old.py')
test_eq((rows[1]['status'], rows[1]['similarity']), ('R', 90))
test_eq(rows[0]['similarity'], 0)
test_eq(_diff_status(''), [])

stats = _diff_numstat('1\t2\ta.py\0-\t-\tbin.png\0')
test_eq(stats['a.py'], {'additions': 1, 'deletions': 2, 'binary': False})
test_eq(stats['bin.png'], {'additions': None, 'deletions': None, 'binary': True})
test_eq(_diff_numstat('3\t4\t\0old.py\0new.py\0')['new.py']['additions'], 3)   # the rename form
test_eq(_diff_numstat(''), {})

test_eq(_summarise_diff([{'additions': 1, 'deletions': 2, 'binary': False},
                         {'additions': None, 'deletions': None, 'binary': True}]),
        {'files': 2, 'additions': 1, 'deletions': 2, 'binary': 1})
test_eq(_summarise_diff([]), {'files': 0, 'additions': 0, 'deletions': 0, 'binary': 0})
```

## Opening a repository

This is where the public API starts.
[`GitRepo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#gitrepo)
holds the root folder of one checkout, and every method from here on
acts on it. `GitRepo.at(path)` accepts any path inside the checkout and
raises
[`GitError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#giterror)
outside one. `run` runs any Git command in the repository and returns
its stdout, for whatever the methods do not cover.

Four private helpers sit behind the methods. `_ask` returns stripped
output, or an empty string when an optional read fails. `_mutate` runs a
command and then clears the cache. `_gitdir` finds the `.git` folder,
and `_version` reads a file as it is in the working tree, the index or
`HEAD`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L532"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.run

``` python
def run(
    *args, **kwargs
):
```

*Run a Git command in this repository and return its stdout.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L525"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.at

``` python
def at(
    path
):
```

*Open the repository that contains `path`, which may be any file or
folder inside it.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L518"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo

``` python
def GitRepo(
    root:Path
)->None:
```

*One local Git checkout, with methods to read it and change it.*

``` python
r = mkrepo()
write(r, 'src/app.py', 'x = 1\n')
test_eq(GitRepo.at(r).root, r.resolve())
test_eq(GitRepo.at(r/'src'/'app.py').root, r.resolve())
test_fail(lambda: GitRepo.at(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())), contains='not inside a Git repository')

repo = GitRepo.at(r)
test_eq(repo.run('branch', '--show-current').strip(), 'main')
test_eq(repo._ask('branch', '--show-current'), 'main')
test_eq(repo._ask('rev-parse', 'nope'), '')             # a read that fails answers with nothing
test_fail(lambda: repo.run('rev-parse', 'nope'))        # ...where `run` still raises
test_eq(repo._mutate('add', '-A'), '')
test_eq(repo._ask('diff', '--cached', '--name-only'), 'src/app.py')

test_eq(repo._gitdir(), r.resolve()/'.git')
test_eq(repo._version('readme.md', 'worktree'), 'hello\n')
test_eq(repo._version('readme.md', 'head'), 'hello\n')
test_eq(repo._version('src/app.py', 'head'), '')        # not committed yet
test_eq(repo._version('missing.txt', 'worktree'), '')
```

## Where the repository is

Three small reads that `info` combines and a caller can also use alone:
the operation in progress and what can be done about it (continue, skip
or abort), the remotes with a web address for each, and the upstream the
current branch tracks together with how many commits each side is ahead.

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
test_eq(r._operation()['active'], '')
test_eq(r._remote_names(), [])
test_eq(r._remotes(), [])
test_eq(r._tracking(), ('', 0, 0))                      # upstream, ahead, behind
test_eq(r._operation()['can_abort'], False)

bare = mkbare()
sh(r.root, 'remote', 'add', 'origin', str(bare))
sh(r.root, 'remote', 'set-url', 'origin', 'git@github.com:o/r.git')
test_eq(r._remote_names(), ['origin'])
test_eq(r._remotes()[0]['name'], 'origin')
test_eq(r._remotes()[0]['web_url'], 'https://github.com/o/r')
sh(r.root, 'remote', 'set-url', 'origin', str(bare))
sh(r.root, 'push', '-u', 'origin', 'main')
commit(r.root, 'ahead', readme__md='ahead\n')
test_eq(r._tracking(), ('origin/main', 1, 0))
```

## Reading changes

`changes` lists every file that differs from the last commit. Each row
has the path, the old path for a rename, Git’s one-letter status for the
index and for the working tree, flags for staged, unstaged, untracked
and conflicted, and line counts for the staged and unstaged parts.
Untracked files are counted by reading them, since Git has no earlier
version to compare with, and a binary file gets `None` counts.

`changes` always reads fresh state, because a caller that asks right
after saving a file has to see the save. `decorations` returns the same
rows through the short-lived cache, for a file tree that asks once per
open folder in a single refresh.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L635"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.decorations

``` python
def decorations():
```

*The same rows as `changes`, through the short-lived cache, for a file
tree that asks repeatedly.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L630"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.changes

``` python
def changes():
```

*Every file that differs from `HEAD`, read fresh on each call.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
test_eq(r.changes(), [])

write(r.root, 'new.txt', 'a\nb\n')
write(r.root, 'readme.md', 'changed\n')
rows = {c['path']: c for c in r.changes()}
test_eq(sorted(rows), ['new.txt', 'readme.md'])
test_eq((rows['new.txt']['untracked'], rows['new.txt']['staged']), (True, False))
test_eq(rows['new.txt']['unstaged_stat'], {'additions': 2, 'deletions': 0, 'binary': False})
test_eq((rows['readme.md']['untracked'], rows['readme.md']['unstaged']), (False, True))
test_eq(rows['readme.md']['unstaged_stat']['additions'], 1)
test_eq(rows['readme.md']['staged_stat'], None)

sh(r.root, 'add', 'readme.md')                          # staged outside the module under test
rows = {c['path']: c for c in r.changes()}
test_eq((rows['readme.md']['staged'], rows['readme.md']['index']), (True, 'M'))
test_eq(rows['readme.md']['staged_stat']['additions'], 1)

write(r.root, 'bin.dat', 'a\0b')
test_eq(first(c for c in r.changes() if c['path'] == 'bin.dat')['unstaged_stat']['binary'], True)
test_eq(len(r.decorations()), len(r.changes()))         # the same answer, one of them cached
```

## What is in the way

Uncommitted changes to tracked files can stop a merge or a rebase from
starting; untracked files usually do not. `_in_the_way` reports those
changes in the form both previews return, so a preview can warn about
them before you start.

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'a.txt': 'a\n'}))
test_eq(r._blocking_changes(), [])
test_eq(r._in_the_way()['clean'], True)

write(r.root, 'a.txt', 'edited\n')
test_eq([c['path'] for c in r._blocking_changes()], ['a.txt'])
test_eq(r._in_the_way()['clean'], False)
test_eq(r._in_the_way()['dirty'], ['a.txt'])

sh(r.root, 'checkout', '--', 'a.txt')
write(r.root, 'untracked.txt', 'new\n')
test_eq(r._in_the_way()['clean'], True)                 # untracked work is not in the way
```

## Preserving uncommitted work

Some operations need a clean working tree. `_set_aside` snapshots the
changes to tracked files, keeps the snapshot under `AUTOSTASH_REF`, and
resets the tree. `_bring_back` reapplies the snapshot after the
operation.

Because the ref keeps the snapshot reachable, nothing is lost when it
cannot be reapplied. In that case `_bring_back` leaves the operation’s
result in place and returns a note with the command that recovers the
work.

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
test_eq(r._set_aside('demo'), '')                       # a clean tree has nothing to set aside

write(r.root, 'readme.md', 'mine\n')
oid = r._set_aside('demo')
assert oid
test_eq((r.root/'readme.md').read_text(), 'hello\n')    # the tree is clean again
test_eq(sh(r.root, 'rev-parse', f'{r.AUTOSTASH_REF}/demo'), oid)

test_eq(r._bring_back(oid), '')
test_eq((r.root/'readme.md').read_text(), 'mine\n')     # ...and the work comes back

# Work that cannot go back on top is kept as a commit, and the note says how to reach it.
r2 = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
write(r2.root, 'readme.md', 'mine\n')
kept = r2._set_aside('demo')
commit(r2.root, 'moved on', readme__md='theirs\n')
note = r2._bring_back(kept)
assert 'git stash apply' in note and kept[:9] in note
test_eq((r2.root/'readme.md').read_text(), 'theirs\n')  # ...and the tree is left consistent
```

## Mutation results

A merge that stops on conflicts has done its job; a person now resolves
them. So `_attempt` returns normally when a command leaves conflicts or
an operation in progress, and raises
[`GitError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/gheasy/repo.html#giterror)
for any other failure. `_guarded` wraps one risky change: it takes the
write lock, records a safepoint, sets uncommitted work aside when asked,
runs the change, brings the work back, and builds the result with
`_outcome`.

That result is the dictionary every guarded method returns. It holds the
operation’s name, Git’s message, the new and the old `HEAD`, whether the
branch moved, the branch, the staged and conflicted files, any operation
in progress, whether uncommitted work was carried across, the `undo`
token with a description of what it undoes, and a one-sentence
`summary`.

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
test_eq(r._attempt('status', '--porcelain=v1'), '')
test_fail(lambda: r._attempt('checkout', 'nope'), contains='did not match')

before = sh(r.root, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD')
out = r._guarded('demo', lambda: r._attempt('commit', '--allow-empty', '-m', 'empty'))
test_eq(out['op'], 'demo')
test_eq(out['branch'], 'main')
test_eq(out['head_before'], before[:9])
test_eq(out['moved'], True)
test_eq((out['staged'], out['conflicted']), ([], []))
test_eq(out['operation']['active'], '')
test_eq(out['summary'], f"demo moved this branch to {out['head']}")
assert out['undo'] and 'demo on main' in out['undoes']
test_eq(gateway().journal(r.root)[0].token, out['undo'])

# A failure inside the guard still raises, and a safepoint is recorded before it does.
test_fail(lambda: r._guarded('bad', lambda: r._attempt('checkout', 'nope')), contains='did not match')
test_eq(gateway().journal(r.root)[0].op, 'bad')

# Work set aside for a mutation that fails is still brought back.
write(r.root, 'readme.md', 'mine\n')
test_fail(lambda: r._guarded('bad', lambda: r._attempt('checkout', 'nope'), autostash=True))
test_eq((r.root/'readme.md').read_text(), 'mine\n')
```

## Undo

`undo` restores a safepoint and `safepoints` lists them, newest first.
`undo()` with no token restores the most recent one, which is what an
Undo button wants.

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L740"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


*The recorded ways back for this repository, newest first.*

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L733"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.undo

``` python
def undo(
    token:str=''
):
```

*Put this repository back where the named safepoint says it was.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
test_eq(r.safepoints(), [])
base = sh(r.root, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD')

r._guarded('one', lambda: r._attempt('commit', '--allow-empty', '-m', 'a'))
r._guarded('two', lambda: r._attempt('commit', '--allow-empty', '-m', 'b'))
test_eq([p['op'] for p in r.safepoints()], ['two', 'one'])
test_eq(len(r.safepoints()[0]['head']), 9)              # shortened for display

test_eq(r.undo()['op'], 'two')                          # no token means the newest
test_eq(r.undo(r.safepoints()[-1]['token'])['op'], 'one')
test_eq(sh(r.root, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'), base)
test_fail(lambda: r.undo('nosuch'), contains='no safepoint nosuch')
```

## Listing branches

`_branches` reads every local and remote branch with one `for-each-ref`
call, newest commit first, with its commit, upstream, how far it is
ahead and behind, author and date. A remote branch that a local branch
already tracks is left out, so main and `origin/main` do not appear as
two entries. Each row also says whether the branch is merged into
`HEAD`, whether it has the newest commit, and whether it is the remote’s
default branch.

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
rows = r._branches()
test_eq([b['name'] for b in rows], ['main'])
main, = rows
test_eq((main['current'], main['remote'], main['upstream']), (True, False, ''))
test_eq((main['ahead'], main['behind'], main['gone']), (0, 0, False))
test_eq((main['merged'], main['latest']), (True, True))
test_eq(main['subject'], 'initial')
test_eq(main['author'], 'Repo tests')

sh(r.root, 'branch', 'feature')
test_eq(sorted(b['name'] for b in r._branches()), ['feature', 'main'])

bare = mkbare()
sh(r.root, 'remote', 'add', 'origin', str(bare))
sh(r.root, 'push', '-u', 'origin', 'main')
commit(r.root, 'ahead one', readme__md='ahead\n')
rows = {b['name']: b for b in r._branches()}
test_eq(rows['main']['upstream'], 'origin/main')
test_eq((rows['main']['ahead'], rows['main']['behind']), (1, 0))
assert 'origin/main' not in rows                        # claimed by a local branch, so not shown twice

sh(r.root, 'push', 'origin', 'main:unclaimed')
sh(r.root, 'fetch', 'origin')
assert 'origin/unclaimed' in {b['name'] for b in r._branches()}
```

## Filters that are configured and missing

A repository can name a filter in `.gitattributes` whose program is not
installed where Git runs. Git does not treat a failing filter as an
error, so the affected files show up as modified again however often
they are staged. `filter_health` checks each filter named in
`.gitattributes`, reports whether it is configured and whether its
program can be found, and explains in plain words what is wrong.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L785"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.filter_health

``` python
def filter_health():
```

*Whether this repository’s content filters can actually run.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
test_eq(r._gitdir(), r.root/'.git')
health = r.filter_health()
test_eq((health['filters'], health['ok'], health['explain']), ([], True, ''))

# The answer is memoised per repository, so each case below gets one of its own.
c = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'.gitattributes': '*.ipynb filter=nbstripout\n'}))
sh(c.root, 'config', 'filter.nbstripout.clean', 'definitely-not-installed')
health = c.filter_health()
test_eq([b['name'] for b in health['filters']], ['nbstripout'])
test_eq((health['ok'], health['filters'][0]['configured']), (False, True))
test_eq(health['filters'][0]['resolved'], '')
assert 'cannot be found' in health['explain']

u = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'.gitattributes': '*.bin filter=missing-test-filter\n'}))
health = u.filter_health()
test_eq([b['name'] for b in health['filters']], ['missing-test-filter'])
test_eq((health['ok'], health['filters'][0]['configured']), (False, False))
assert 'configured nowhere' in health['explain']
```

## Staging

Staging means choosing which changes go into the next commit; Git keeps
the chosen versions in the index. `stage` adds files to the index and
`unstage` takes them out again. `discard` throws away unstaged edits in
the working tree, and this cannot be undone. `ignore` adds a path to
`.gitignore` without writing the same rule twice. `write_worktree`
writes a file inside the repository and refuses paths outside it.
`apply_patch` applies a unified diff, such as one hunk picked in a diff
view, to the index by default, or to the working tree with
`staged=False`; `reverse=True` takes the patch back out.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L847"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
test_fail(lambda: r.write_worktree('../escape.txt', 'x'), contains='outside')
test_fail(lambda: r.write_worktree('nowhere/b.txt', 'x'), contains='does not exist')

r.apply_patch(_unified('hello\n', 'patched\n', 'a/readme.md', 'b/readme.md'))
test_eq(r._ask('show', ':readme.md'), 'patched')        # staged by default: the index moves
test_eq((r.root/'readme.md').read_text(), 'hello\n')    # ...and the worktree does not
test_fail(lambda: r.apply_patch('  '), contains='at least one diff hunk')
```

## Switching branches

`checkout` switches to a local branch or a remote branch such as
`origin/feature`. For a remote branch it creates a local branch that
tracks it, or switches to the existing one and sets its upstream.

Git refuses to switch when the switch would overwrite uncommitted
changes. `checkout` then sets the changes aside, switches, and puts them
back. If they conflict with what is on the target branch, it switches
back and restores the work, so you end up where you started with nothing
lost.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L873"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.checkout

``` python
def checkout(
    branch
):
```

*Switch branches, setting aside uncommitted work only if Git refuses to
carry it.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
assert r._has_ref('refs/heads/main')
assert not r._has_ref('refs/heads/nope')

sh(r.root, 'branch', 'feature')
out = r.checkout('feature')
test_eq(r.run('branch', '--show-current').strip(), 'feature')
test_eq(out['op'], 'checkout')
test_fail(lambda: r.checkout('nope'), contains='nope')

bare = mkbare()
sh(r.root, 'remote', 'add', 'origin', str(bare))
sh(r.root, 'push', 'origin', 'main:published')
sh(r.root, 'fetch', 'origin')
r.checkout('origin/published')
test_eq(r.run('branch', '--show-current').strip(), 'published')
test_eq(r._tracking()[0], 'origin/published')

# Uncommitted work the switch cannot carry leaves the repository exactly where it was.
r.checkout('main')
commit(r.root, 'diverge', readme__md='on main\n')
r.checkout('feature')
write(r.root, 'readme.md', 'in progress\n')
test_fail(lambda: r.checkout('main'), contains='you are still on feature with your work')
test_eq(r.run('branch', '--show-current').strip(), 'feature')
test_eq((r.root/'readme.md').read_text(), 'in progress\n')

# ...and work that has nowhere to clash comes across with it.
r.discard(['readme.md'])
write(r.root, 'scratch.txt', 'notes\n')
r.stage(['scratch.txt'])
r.checkout('main')
test_eq(r.run('branch', '--show-current').strip(), 'main')
test_eq((r.root/'scratch.txt').read_text(), 'notes\n')
```

## Other branch commands

The rest of `git branch`, one method each. `create` makes a branch and
switches to it. `rename_branch`, `set_upstream` and `unset_upstream`
change a branch’s name or the remote branch it tracks. `delete` removes
a local branch, and with `force=True` it does so even when the branch is
not merged. `delete_remote` deletes a branch on a remote; it is a push,
so it gets the two-minute timeout network commands use.

``` python
sh(r.root, 'push', 'origin', 'main:doomed')
sh(r.root, 'fetch', 'origin')
r.delete_remote('origin', 'doomed')
assert 'doomed' not in sh(bare, 'branch', '--list')
```

## Commit, and the remote

`commit` and `pull` are guarded and return the result dictionary;
`fetch` and `push` return Git’s output as text. `commit` refuses an
empty message, and `amend=True` replaces the last commit. `fetch`
fetches from one remote or all of them, and by default prunes branches
deleted on the remote. `pull` only fast-forwards. When your branch has
commits the upstream lacks, it fails rather than making a merge commit
you did not ask for; `divergence` and `sync` handle that case. `push`
with `publish=True` pushes a branch that has no upstream yet and sets
one, using `origin` when it exists. `force_with_lease=True` overwrites
the remote branch, but only if nobody has pushed to it since you last
fetched.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L938"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

*Push this branch; `publish` sets an upstream for a new branch and
`force_with_lease` overwrites only an unchanged remote.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
write(r.root, 'a.txt', 'a\n')
r.stage(['a.txt'])
out = r.commit('add a')
test_eq(out['op'], 'commit')
test_eq(out['moved'], True)
test_eq(r._ask('log', '-1', '--format=%s'), 'add a')

r.commit('add a, said better', amend=True)
test_eq(r._ask('log', '-1', '--format=%s'), 'add a, said better')

bare = mkbare()
sh(r.root, 'remote', 'add', 'origin', str(bare))
r.push(publish=True)                                    # `push` and `fetch` report as text
test_eq(r._tracking()[0], 'origin/main')
r.fetch()
test_eq(r.pull()['op'], 'pull')                         # ...and `pull` as an outcome, being guarded
test_fail(lambda: GitRepo.at(mkrepo()).push(publish=True), contains='add a remote')

# A second clone commits, and the first pulls it down as a fast-forward.
other = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); _tmp.append(str(other))
o = GitRepo.at(clone(str(bare), other, 'other'))
sh(o.root, 'config', 'user.email', 'tests@example.com')
sh(o.root, 'config', 'user.name', 'Repo tests')
commit(o.root, 'from the other clone', b__txt='b\n')
o.push()
test_eq(r.pull()['moved'], True)
test_eq((r.root/'b.txt').read_text(), 'b\n')
```

## Stash

A stash puts uncommitted work on a shelf and cleans the working tree.
`stash` includes untracked files, since new files are often part of the
work. `stash_pop` reapplies a stash and removes it from the list,
`stash_apply` reapplies it and keeps it, and `stash_drop` deletes it.
Each takes a ref such as `stash@{1}`, so an interface can act on any
entry in the list and not only the newest.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L965"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
write(r.root, 'readme.md', 'in progress\n')
write(r.root, 'untracked.txt', 'also\n')
r.stash('wip')
test_eq((r.root/'readme.md').read_text(), 'hello\n')
assert not (r.root/'untracked.txt').exists()            # -u: untracked work is work
assert 'wip' in sh(r.root, 'stash', 'list')

r.stash_pop()
test_eq((r.root/'readme.md').read_text(), 'in progress\n')
test_eq(sh(r.root, 'stash', 'list'), '')

r.stash('again')
r.stash_apply()
test_eq((r.root/'readme.md').read_text(), 'in progress\n')
assert 'again' in sh(r.root, 'stash', 'list')           # applied, not popped
r.stash_drop()
test_eq(sh(r.root, 'stash', 'list'), '')
```

## Bringing work together

`merge`, `rebase`, `cherry_pick`, `revert` and `reset` are all guarded,
and a conflict comes back as a result rather than an exception: the
conflicted files are listed and the operation is left in progress.
`merge` takes a strategy: `merge`, `squash` (stage the combined changes
without committing them) or `ff-only`, and it sets uncommitted work
aside while it runs. `rebase` replays your commits on top of another
branch, `cherry_pick` copies one commit onto the current branch, and
`revert` adds a commit that undoes one. `reset` moves the branch to
another commit; `soft` keeps the changes staged, `mixed` keeps them
unstaged, and `hard` discards them. When one of these stops on a
conflict, `operation_action` continues, skips or aborts it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1001"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
sh(r.root, 'branch', 'feature')
commit(r.root, 'on main', main__txt='main\n')
r.checkout('feature')
commit(r.root, 'on feature', feature__txt='feature\n')

out = r.merge('main')
test_eq(out['op'], 'merge')
test_eq(out['conflicted'], [])
assert (r.root/'main.txt').exists()

# A conflict is an outcome: the files are named and the operation is left in progress.
c = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'shared.txt': 'base\n'}))
sh(c.root, 'branch', 'other')
commit(c.root, 'ours', shared__txt='ours\n')
c.checkout('other')
commit(c.root, 'theirs', shared__txt='theirs\n')
out = c.merge('main')
test_eq(out['conflicted'], ['shared.txt'])
test_eq(out['operation']['active'], 'merge')
assert 'resolve them to continue' in out['summary']
aborted = c.operation_action('abort')
test_eq((aborted['op'], aborted['operation']['active']), ('merge --abort', ''))

test_fail(lambda: c.operation_action('abort'), contains='no Git operation is in progress')
test_fail(lambda: c.merge('main', 'sideways'), contains='merge strategy must be')

r2 = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
sh(r2.root, 'branch', 'topic')
commit(r2.root, 'on main', m__txt='m\n')
r2.checkout('topic')
commit(r2.root, 'on topic', t__txt='t\n')
test_eq(r2.rebase('main')['op'], 'rebase')
test_eq(r2._ask('log', '--format=%s', '-3').splitlines(), ['on topic', 'on main', 'initial'])

pick = r2._ask('rev-parse', 'main')
r2.checkout('main')
test_eq(r2.revert(r2._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD'))['op'], 'revert')
assert not (r2.root/'m.txt').exists()

head = r2._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD')
test_eq(r2.reset('HEAD~1', 'hard')['op'], 'reset')
test_ne(r2._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD'), head)
test_fail(lambda: r2.reset('HEAD', 'sideways'), contains='mode')

r3 = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
sh(r3.root, 'branch', 'side')
commit(r3.root, 'on main', only__txt='only\n')
target = r3._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD')
r3.checkout('side')
test_eq(r3.cherry_pick(target)['op'], 'cherry-pick')
assert (r3.root/'only.txt').exists()
```

## Repository status for an interface

`info` returns everything an editor’s Git panel shows: the current
branch, how far it is ahead of and behind its upstream, the branches,
remotes, changes, stashes and tags, any operation in progress, the time
of the last fetch, filter health, and recent safepoints. The separate
reads run at the same time on a small shared pool of threads. The result
is cached for under a second, so the parts of one panel refresh share
it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1058"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.info

``` python
def info():
```

*Everything an editor’s Git panel shows for this repository, in one
dictionary, cached briefly.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
d = r.info()
test_eq(d['root'], str(r.root))
test_eq(d['branch'], 'main')
test_eq((d['clean'], d['upstream'], d['ahead'], d['behind']), (True, '', 0, 0))
test_eq([b['name'] for b in d['branches']], ['main'])
test_eq((d['changes'], d['remotes']), ([], []))
test_eq(d['operation']['active'], '')
test_eq(r._fetch_time(), 0)                             # nothing has been fetched yet

write(r.root, 'readme.md', 'changed\n')
test_eq(r.info()['clean'], True)                        # `info` is cached for less than a second
invalidate(r.root)
test_eq(r.info()['clean'], False)
test_eq([c['path'] for c in r.info()['changes']], ['readme.md'])

bare = mkbare()
sh(r.root, 'remote', 'add', 'origin', str(bare))
sh(r.root, 'push', '-u', 'origin', 'main')
sh(r.root, 'fetch', 'origin')
invalidate(r.root)
test_eq(r.info()['upstream'], 'origin/main')
assert r._fetch_time() > 0                              # ...and now something has
```

## Compact repository status

`brief` is the one-row version of `info`, for prompts, status bars and
tables of many repositories. It has the branch and how far it is ahead
and behind, counts of staged, unstaged, untracked and conflicted files,
the last commit, the latest tag and how many commits have landed since
it, any operation in progress, and the `origin` URL. Pass `fresh=True`
to skip the cache.

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo()); bar = threading.Barrier(2)
def meet(real, argv, *a, **k):
    if {'tag', 'stash'} & set(argv): bar.wait(timeout=5)
    return real(argv, *a, **k)
with hook_run(meet): d = r.info()
test_eq(d['branch'], 'main')                            # `stash list` and `tag -l` were inside git together
```

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo()); out = []
def inside():
    with gateway()._lock(r.root).write(): out.append(r.info()['branch'])
t = threading.Thread(target=inside, daemon=True); t.start(); t.join(5)
test_eq(out, ['main'])                                  # inside its own write it collects serially
invalidate(r.root)
test_eq(_pool().submit(r.info).result(timeout=5)['branch'], 'main')   # ...and so does a pool worker
```

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo()); fired = []
def save_during(real, argv, *a, **k):
    if 'tag' in argv and not fired: fired.append(1); write(r.root, 'saved.txt', 'x\n'); invalidate(r.root)
    return real(argv, *a, **k)
with hook_run(save_during): r.info()
test_eq([c['path'] for c in r.info()['changes']], ['saved.txt'])   # an answer begun before the save was not kept
```

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo()); tag_failed = threading.Event()
def broken(real, argv, *a, **k):
    if 'tag' in argv: tag_failed.set(); return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 1, '', 'tag boom')
    if 'stash' in argv: tag_failed.wait(.5); return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 1, '', 'stash boom')
    return real(argv, *a, **k)
with hook_run(broken): test_fail(r.info, contains='stash boom')   # the first failure in the old order, not in time
```

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo()); invalidate(r.root); r.info()
k, c = (str(r.root), 'info'), (str(r.root), 'changes')
test_eq(c in _CACHE, True)                              # a miss seeds the file tree's answer
_CACHE[k] = (time.monotonic(), _CACHE[k][1]); _CACHE[c] = (time.monotonic(), 'kept')
r.info()
test_eq(_CACHE[c][1], 'kept')                           # a hit leaves it alone
invalidate(r.root)
```

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo()); invalidate(r.root); gateway()._env_cache.clear()
seen = []
with spy_exec(seen): r.info()
test_eq(sum(any(a in ('--git-dir', '--git-path') for a in args) for _, args in seen), 1)   # one layout lookup, not four
```

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

*This repository as one row: branch, ahead and behind, uncommitted

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
b = r.brief()
test_eq((b['branch'], b['clean'], b['changed']), ('main', True, 0))
test_eq(b['name'], r.root.name)
test_eq(b['last_commit']['subject'], 'initial')

write(r.root, 'readme.md', 'changed\n')

b = r.brief(fresh=True)
test_eq((b['clean'], b['changed'], b['unstaged']), (False, 1, 1))
```

## History

`history` lists commits newest first, from every branch by default.
`ref` limits it to a branch or a range such as `main..feature`, `query`
keeps commits whose message matches, ignoring case, and `path` keeps
commits that touched one file. `limit` and `skip` page through the
results, at most 500 at a time. `reflog` lists the commits `HEAD` has
pointed at, which is how you find a commit again after a reset.
`commit_detail` returns one commit with its full message and patch.
`_resolve_ref` turns a branch, tag or commit name into a full commit id,
and refuses names that start with `-`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1161"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo())
second = commit(r.root, 'the second commit', a__txt='a\n')
rows = r.history()
test_eq([x['subject'] for x in rows], ['the second commit', 'initial'])
test_eq(rows[0]['short'], second)
test_eq(rows[0]['author'], 'Repo tests')
test_eq(len(rows[0]['oid']), 40)

test_eq(len(r.history(limit=1)), 1)
test_eq([x['subject'] for x in r.history(skip=1)], ['initial'])
test_eq([x['subject'] for x in r.history(query='second')], ['the second commit'])
test_eq([x['subject'] for x in r.history(path='a.txt')], ['the second commit'])
test_eq(r.history(ref='HEAD~1..HEAD')[0]['subject'], 'the second commit')

assert r.reflog()
test_eq(r.reflog(limit=1) and len(r.reflog(limit=1)), 1)

d = r.commit_detail('HEAD')
test_eq(d['message'], 'the second commit')
test_eq(d['short'], second)
test_eq(d['parents'], [r.history()[-1]['oid']])
assert 'a.txt' in d['patch']

test_eq(len(r._resolve_ref('HEAD')), 40)
test_eq(r._resolve_ref('HEAD~1'), r.history()[-1]['oid'])
test_fail(lambda: r._resolve_ref('nope'), contains='unknown branch, tag, or commit')
test_fail(lambda: r._resolve_ref(''), contains='choose a branch')
test_fail(lambda: r._resolve_ref('--upload-pack=evil'), contains='unknown branch')
```

## Comparing refs safely

A ref is any name Git resolves to a commit: a branch, a tag or a commit
id. `_diff_files` returns one record per changed file between two refs,
with renames detected and line counts filled in. `_merge_tree` rehearses
a merge with `git merge-tree --write-tree`. That may add objects to
Git’s store, but it changes no ref, the index or the working tree.

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'a.txt': 'one\n'}))
base = r._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD')
commit(r.root, 'change a, add b', a__txt='two\n', b__txt='b\n')
rows = {x['path']: x for x in r._diff_files(base, 'HEAD')}
test_eq(sorted(rows), ['a.txt', 'b.txt'])
test_eq((rows['a.txt']['additions'], rows['a.txt']['deletions']), (1, 1))
test_eq(rows['b.txt']['status'], 'A')

m = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'shared.txt': 'base\n'}))
sh(m.root, 'branch', 'other')
commit(m.root, 'ours', shared__txt='ours\n')
ours = m._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD')
m.checkout('other')
commit(m.root, 'theirs', shared__txt='theirs\n')
theirs = m._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD')

tree, files, clashed = m._merge_tree(ours, theirs)
test_eq((files, clashed), (['shared.txt'], True))
assert tree
test_eq(m._rehearse(ours, theirs), (['shared.txt'], True))
test_eq(m._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD'), theirs)            # rehearsing moved nothing

clean = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'a.txt': 'a\n'}))
sh(clean.root, 'branch', 'other')
commit(clean.root, 'ours', a__txt='ours\n')
o = clean._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD')
clean.checkout('other')
commit(clean.root, 'theirs', b__txt='b\n')
test_eq(clean._rehearse(o, 'HEAD'), ([], False))
```

## Reviewing a comparison

`review(base, head)` describes everything that differs between two refs:
one record per file with its status and line counts, the commits on
`head` that `base` lacks, how many commits each side has that the other
does not, and totals. The default, `mode='review'`, compares `head` with
the merge base, which shows what the branch itself changed.
`mode='snapshot'` compares the two trees as they stand now, which also
counts changes made on `base`. When review mode finds nothing but the
trees do differ, `snapshot_alternative` holds the snapshot totals so a
viewer can offer to switch. `can_apply` is true when `base` is the
current commit, `head` builds on it, and nothing is uncommitted.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1220"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.review

``` python
def review(
    base, head, mode:str='review'
):
```

*Per-file review metadata: `review` compares the merge base, `snapshot`
the whole trees.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'a.txt': 'one\n'}))
base = r._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD')
commit(r.root, 'change a, add b', a__txt='two\n', b__txt='b\n')

rev = r.review(base, 'HEAD')
test_eq(sorted(f['path'] for f in rev['files']), ['a.txt', 'b.txt'])
test_eq(rev['summary'], {'files': 2, 'additions': 2, 'deletions': 1, 'binary': 0})
test_eq((rev['base_only'], rev['head_only']), (0, 1))
test_eq(rev['merge_base'], base)
test_eq([c['subject'] for c in rev['commits']], ['change a, add b'])
test_fail(lambda: r.review(base, 'HEAD', 'sideways'), contains='review or snapshot')
```

## One file of a comparison

`review_file` returns both versions of one file from a `review`
comparison, and the patch between them. A viewer calls it when a file is
opened, rather than loading every file up front. For a notebook, both
sides are its cell sources rather than raw JSON.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1261"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.review_file

``` python

    base, head, path, mode:str='review', context:int=3
):
```

*Both versions of `path` in a `review` comparison, and the patch between
them.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'a.txt': 'one\n'}))
base = r._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD')
commit(r.root, 'change a, add b', a__txt='two\n', b__txt='b\n')

one = r.review_file(base, 'HEAD', 'a.txt')
test_eq(one['file']['path'], 'a.txt')
test_eq((one['left'], one['right']), ('one\n', 'two\n'))
assert '+two' in one['patch']

test_eq(r._ref_file(base, 'a.txt'), 'one\n')
test_eq(r._ref_file(base, 'nothere.txt'), '')           # a file that was not there reads as empty
test_eq(r._ref_file('', 'a.txt'), '')
test_eq(r.review_file(base, 'HEAD', 'b.txt')['left'], '')
test_fail(lambda: r.review_file(base, 'HEAD', 'readme.md'), contains='not changed')
```

## Reviewing one commit

`commit_review` and `commit_file` give the same view for a single commit
compared with its parent. A repository’s first commit has no parent, so
it is compared with an empty tree.

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'a.txt': 'one\n'}))
commit(r.root, 'change a, add b', a__txt='two\n', b__txt='b\n')

d = r.commit_review('HEAD')
test_eq(d['message'], 'change a, add b')
test_eq(sorted(f['path'] for f in d['files']), ['a.txt', 'b.txt'])
test_eq(d['summary']['files'], 2)
assert 'patch' not in d                                 # the per-file records replace it
test_eq(r.commit_file('HEAD', 'a.txt')['right'], 'two\n')
test_eq(r.commit_file('HEAD', 'a.txt')['left'], 'one\n')
test_fail(lambda: r.commit_file('HEAD', 'nothere.txt'), contains='not changed by this commit')

root = r.commit_review(r.history()[-1]['oid'])          # the first commit, against the empty tree
test_eq([f['path'] for f in root['files']], ['a.txt'])
test_eq(r.commit_file(r.history()[-1]['oid'], 'a.txt')['left'], '')
```

## Previewing integration

`merge_preview(incoming)` describes merging a branch into the current
one, without changing anything. It reports how the two relate
(`identical`, `fast-forward`, `already-merged` or `diverged`), which
files would conflict, any uncommitted changes in the way, and a full
`review` of what would come in. `rebase_preview(onto)` describes
rebasing the current branch onto another: the commits that would be
replayed, the files that would conflict, and whether the branch already
starts from `onto`. `compare` returns the plain difference between the
full trees at two refs, as a patch with counts.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1329"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'a.txt': 'a\n'}))
sh(r.root, 'branch', 'other')

r.checkout('other')

test_eq(r._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD'), head)              # rehearsing moved nothing
test_eq(r.rebase_preview('main')['conflicts'], [])
test_eq(r.rebase_preview('main')['already_based'], False)
cmp = r.compare('main', 'other')                        # whole trees, not the merge base
test_eq(cmp['changed_files'], 2)
test_eq((cmp['left_only'], cmp['right_only']), (1, 1))

c = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'shared.txt': 'base\n'}))
sh(c.root, 'branch', 'other')

c.checkout('other')

test_eq(c.merge_preview('main')['conflict_likely'], True)
test_eq(c._ask('rev-parse', 'HEAD'), c._ask('rev-parse', 'other'))
```

## Resolving one conflict

`conflict_versions` returns the versions of a conflicted file: `base`,
the common ancestor; `ours` and `theirs`, the two sides; and `worktree`,
the file on disk with its conflict markers. `resolve_conflict` settles
the file by taking `ours`, `theirs`, the working-tree file as it is, or
text you pass with `'resolved'`, and then stages it. The result lists
the files still conflicted.

During a merge, `ours` is the branch you have checked out and `theirs`
is the branch coming in.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1352"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python

    path, choice, content:NoneType=None
):
```

*Settle one conflicted file and stage it as resolved.*

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1341"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.conflict_versions

``` python
def conflict_versions(
    path
):
```

*The base, ours, theirs and working-tree versions of the conflicted file
`path`.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'shared.txt': 'base\n'}))
sh(r.root, 'branch', 'other')
commit(r.root, 'ours', shared__txt='ours\n')
r.checkout('other')
commit(r.root, 'theirs', shared__txt='theirs\n')
r.merge('main')

v = r.conflict_versions('shared.txt')
test_eq((v['ours'], v['theirs'], v['base']), ('theirs\n', 'ours\n', 'base\n'))

out = r.resolve_conflict('shared.txt', 'ours')
test_eq((r.root/'shared.txt').read_text(), 'theirs\n')
test_eq(out['conflicted'], [])
test_eq(out['operation']['active'], 'merge')            # resolved, but not yet committed
assert 'every conflict is resolved' in out['summary']
r.operation_action('abort')

r.merge('main')
r.resolve_conflict('shared.txt', 'theirs')
test_eq((r.root/'shared.txt').read_text(), 'ours\n')
r.operation_action('abort')

r.merge('main')
r.resolve_conflict('shared.txt', 'resolved', 'decided by hand\n')
test_eq((r.root/'shared.txt').read_text(), 'decided by hand\n')
r.operation_action('abort')

r.merge('main')
test_fail(lambda: r.resolve_conflict('shared.txt', 'nonsense'), contains='conflict choice must be')
test_fail(lambda: r.resolve_conflict('shared.txt', 'resolved'), contains='resolved contents')
test_fail(lambda: r.conflict_versions('readme.md'), contains='is not conflicted')
r.operation_action('abort')
```

## Planning conflict resolution

A conflict block whose two sides are identical needs no decision.
`resolve_safe_conflicts` removes the markers around such blocks, and
stages a file once none of its blocks remain. Blocks whose sides differ
are left for a person. `conflict_plan` lists the conflicted files with
how many blocks each has and how many of those are safe in this sense; a
binary file is marked as needing one whole side chosen.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1392"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.resolve_safe_conflicts

``` python
def resolve_safe_conflicts(
    paths:tuple=()
):
```

*Remove only conflict markers whose ours and theirs text is identical,
then stage.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1371"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.conflict_plan

``` python
def conflict_plan():
```

*Unresolved files with deterministic marker-level resolution
suggestions.*

``` python
r = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'shared.txt': 'base\n'}))
sh(r.root, 'branch', 'other')
commit(r.root, 'ours', shared__txt='ours\n')
r.checkout('other')
commit(r.root, 'theirs', shared__txt='theirs\n')
r.merge('main')

plan = r.conflict_plan()
test_eq([f['path'] for f in plan['files']], ['shared.txt'])
test_eq(plan['operation']['active'], 'merge')
test_eq(plan['files'][0]['kind'], 'text')
test_eq((plan['files'][0]['blocks'], plan['files'][0]['safe']), (1, 0))
test_eq(plan['summary'], {'files': 1, 'blocks': 1, 'safe': 0, 'manual': 1})

# Two sides that genuinely differ are nobody's to resolve automatically, so nothing is taken.
test_eq(r.resolve_safe_conflicts()['resolved'], [])
test_eq([f['path'] for f in r.resolve_safe_conflicts()['plan']['files']], ['shared.txt'])

# A block whose two sides say the same thing is safe, and taking it stages the file.
s = GitRepo.at(mkrepo({'both.txt': 'a\nb\nc\n'}))
sh(s.root, 'branch', 'other')
commit(s.root, 'ours', both__txt='a\nb\nOURS\n')
s.checkout('other')
commit(s.root, 'theirs', both__txt='a\nb\nTHEIRS\n')
s.merge('main')
marked = s._version('both.txt', 'worktree')
block, = _conflict_blocks(marked)
s.write_worktree('both.txt', marked[:block['start']] + '<<<<<<< HEAD\nsame\n=======\nsame\n'
                 '>>>>>>> main\n' + marked[block['end']:])
done = s.resolve_safe_conflicts()
test_eq([x['path'] for x in done['resolved']], ['both.txt'])
test_eq((done['resolved'][0]['safe'], done['resolved'][0]['remaining']), (1, 0))
test_eq(done['plan']['files'], [])
test_eq((s.root/'both.txt').read_text(), 'a\nb\nsame\n')

r.operation_action('abort')
test_eq(r.conflict_plan()['files'], [])                 # nothing in progress, nothing to decide
```

``` python
rows = r.blame('a.txt')
test_eq(len(rows), 2)
```

## Worktrees and submodules

A worktree is an extra checkout of the same repository in another
folder, usually with a different branch checked out. A submodule is
another repository embedded in this one at a fixed commit. `worktrees`
lists the checkouts, `add_worktree` creates one (and with `create=True`
creates `branch` too), and `remove_worktree` deletes one. `submodules`
lists the submodules with the commit each is at.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/gheasy/blob/main/gheasy/repo.py#L1471"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### GitRepo.submodules

``` python
def submodules():
```

*The submodules, each with its path, commit and state.*
